question: Administering high-flow oxygen (FiO2 > 0.35) via a non-rebreather mask to a COPD patient with chronic hypercapnia carries a risk of worsening hypercapnia by abolishing the hypoxic ventilatory drive.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. High-flow oxygen in hypercapnic COPD can suppress the residual hypoxic ventilatory drive, worsen CO2 retention, and precipitate respiratory acidosis. Always titrate oxygen to SpO2 88–92% in known COPD.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. In chronically hypercapnic COPD patients, the hypoxic drive is a significant contributor to ventilation. Excessive oxygen abolishes this drive, risks CO2 narcosis, and is why the target SpO2 in COPD is 88–92% rather than >94%.
